topic_name: Number Play: Will It Always Happen?
title: Signs between four numbers, always even?
description: Shows two tries of placing signs between four consecutive numbers, both giving even results, and asks if this always happens.

title: Fifteen written three ways
description: Shows that one number, 15, can be written as a sum of consecutive numbers in more than one way.

title: Eight ways to place three signs
description: Shows that three gaps with two sign choices each give 2 × 2 × 2 = 8 expressions for 3, 4, 5, 6, and every result is even.

title: Switch one sign, the value moves by 2 × 4
description: Shows that switching one sign changes the value by twice the switched number, so the parity stays the same.

title: Switching signs moves the total by an even amount
description: Shows that switching the signs of 7 and 9 in 2 + 7 + 4 + 9 + 6 changes the total from 28 to −4, a change of 2 × 16 = 32, so the parity stays even.

title: Four cards, three sign switches
description: Shows the sign flip board in its simplest state: four number cards, a sign switch in each gap, and the result with its parity.

title: Parity rules for sums and differences
description: Shows the rule table odd ± odd is even, even ± even is even, odd ± even is odd, applied to 543 − 479.

title: A factor of 2 means always even
description: Shows that 4m + 2q can be rewritten as 2 times something, so it is even for every integer m and q.

title: Always even, or not always?
description: Shows the core move of the practice: factor out 2 to prove always even, or find one value that gives an odd result.

title: Full rows of four, or two left over
description: Shows the two kinds of even numbers: multiples of 4 fill rows of four, the others leave 2 dots over.

title: Two leftover pairs make one more row of four
description: Shows 22 as 5 rows of 4 with 2 left and 6 as 1 row of 4 with 2 left; the two leftover pairs join into one full row, so 22 + 6 = 28 = 4 × 7.

title: Multiple of 4 plus 4q + 2 leaves 2 over
description: Shows that adding a multiple of 4 to an even number that is not one always leaves 2 dots over.

title: Rows of 8 stay rows of 8
description: Shows 16 as 2 rows of 8 and 56 as 7 rows of 8 stacked into 9 rows of 8, so 16 + 56 = 72 = 8 × 9.

title: 42 in rows of 7: groups of 14 fit, groups of 28 do not
description: Shows that a multiple of 7 is divisible by another multiple of 7 only sometimes: 42 splits into groups of 14 but not into groups of 28.

title: Divisible by 6 and by 4 means divisible by 12
description: Shows on a number line that the numbers divisible by both 6 and 4 come every 12, not every 24.

title: Odd plus even always leaves one unpaired
description: Shows that an odd number plus an even number is odd, so it can never be a multiple of 6, which is even.

title: Always, sometimes or never
description: Shows the core move of the practice: sorting a statement as always, sometimes or never true, with one short reason for each.

title: Three more than a multiple of 5
description: Shows that numbers leaving remainder 3 on division by 5 sit 3 steps after each multiple of 5, giving 5k + 3.

title: Only the remainders matter
description: Shows 17 as 3 groups of 5 with 2 loose and 24 as 4 groups of 5 with 4 loose; the 6 loose dots make one more group and leave 1, so 17 + 24 leaves remainder 1.

title: Remainder 1 on division by 2 and by 3
description: Shows that numbers leaving remainder 1 on division by both 2 and 3 repeat every 6, as 6k + 1.

title: Every 12 from 2
description: Shows the numbers that leave remainder 2 on division by 3 and by 4 as equal jumps of 12 from 2: the form 12k + 2.

topic_name: Why the Shortcuts for 10, 5, 2, 4 and 8 Work
title: 4075 as a sum of place values
description: Shows that every place value except the units is a multiple of 10, so only the units digit decides divisibility by 10.

topic_name: Why the Shortcuts for 10, 5, 2, 4 and 8 Work
title: Every place but the units is a multiple of 10
description: Shows 3716 split into 3000 + 700 + 10 + 6, where every part except the units digit is a multiple of 10, so only 6 decides divisibility by 2 and 5.

topic_name: Why the Shortcuts for 10, 5, 2, 4 and 8 Work
title: Divisor 4: only the last two digits decide
description: Shows the rule bench in its simplest state: with divisor 4, the thousands and hundreds blocks are shaded as multiples of 4 and only the last two digits are left to test.

title: A number made of nines and zeros
description: Shows 99009 as 9 × 10000 + 9 × 1000 + 9 × 1, each part a multiple of 9, so the number is a multiple of 9.

title: Each place value is nines plus one
description: Shows that each hundred is 99 plus 1 and each ten is 9 plus 1, so the leftovers of 427 are its digits.

title: A number and its digit sum share a remainder
description: Shows 7309 and its digit sum 19 both leave remainder 1 on division by 9, and 4581 and 18 both leave remainder 0.

title: Why 87 passes the test for 3
description: Shows that each ten is 9 plus 1, so 87 leaves the same remainder on division by 3 as 8 + 7 = 15.

title: Split the blocks, gather the ones
description: Shows the core move of the nines and ones tool: 427 split into blocks of nines plus loose ones, the 13 loose ones losing one group of 9 to leave remainder 4.

title: 462: one more, one less, one more
description: Shows that hundreds and units are one more than a multiple of 11 and tens one less, so 462 is a multiple of 11.

title: Excess minus shortfall
description: Shows 320185 with its digits sorted into excess places and shortfall places: 8 − 11 = −3, so the remainder on division by 11 is 8.

title: Alternating signs on 328105
description: Shows the alternating sign procedure: signs alternate from the units digit, and the total gives the remainder on division by 11.

title: Alternate the signs from the units digit
description: Shows the test for 11 on 5529: +9 − 2 + 5 − 5 = 7, so the remainder is 7.

title: 186 passes the tests for 2 and 3
description: Shows that a number divisible by 2 and by 3 is divisible by 6, using 186.

title: 4 and 6 share a 2, 8 and 3 share nothing
description: Compares factor tiles: 4 and 6 overlap on one 2 and only cover 12, while 8 and 3 share nothing and cover all of 24.

title: 12 slips through 4 and 6 but not 24
description: Shows the combined divisibility trap in its simplest state: 12 passes the gates for 4 and 6 but fails the gate for 24.

title: Keep adding the digits
description: Shows 489710 reducing to its digital root: digit sum 29, then 11, then 2.

title: Digital root 5 between 600 and 700
description: Shows that numbers with the same digital root step up in nines, starting from 608.

title: Digital roots go round in a cycle
description: Shows the digital roots of 7, 13, 19, 25, 31 cycling 7, 4, 1 on a ring of the nine roots.

title: Nine ones
description: Shows the answer to the riddle: nine digits, each 1, with digit sum 9 and digital root 9.

title: Add 10, the root goes up by 1
description: Shows the core move of the practice: adding 10, whose digital root is 1, raises a digital root of 5 to 6.

title: Start with the units column
description: Shows how the units column fixes B and the carry fixes A in A1 + 1B = B0.

title: The product must stay two digits
description: Shows that PQ × 8 = RS forces PQ to be at most 12, and 12 × 8 = 96 is the answer.

title: The multiplier H matches the units digit
description: Shows that in GH × H = 9K the multiplier must equal the units digit of GH, picking 24 × 4 = 96.

title: BYE × 6 = RAY solved
description: Shows the solved puzzle 105 × 6 = 630 with each letter matched to its digit.

title: Drop a digit, every copy fills
description: Shows the digit puzzle solver in its simplest state: A is set to 2 in both places in AB + 37 = 6A, and a digit is dragged onto B.

title: Three things we found
description: A clean summary of three findings: a sign switch changes the result by an even amount, divisible by two numbers means divisible by their LCM, and every place value is a multiple of 9 plus 1.

title: Navakankari: a line of three
description: Shows the Navakankari board and the goal of the game: three pawns in a line.
